name: Venetian Dalmatia
alt: Provveditore generale in Dalmazia e Albania

predecessors.name: Croatia in union with Hungary
predecessors.text: Zadar and its neighbourhood, bought with Ladislaus's rights in 1409

successors.name: Habsburg monarchy
successors.text: "Venetian Istria, Venetian Dalmatia and the Bay of Kotor region were turned over to the Habsburg emperor" by the Treaty of Campo Formio, 17 October 1797

ledger.x: 1409: Ladislaus of Naples sells his rights on Dalmatia to Venice for 100,000 ducats, the start of the Venetian rule the page dates "between 1409 and 1797".
1409: bridged from the purchase; the page names no campaign in Dalmatia before 1420, only Venice's victory over Sigismund's forces at the Battle of Motta in 1412.
1420: the Dalmatian coast is Venetian.
1420: Venice holds the coastal cities except Ragusa and the contest with Sigismund ends.
1420: Venice "did not permanently assume control until 1420".
1480: Krk becomes Venetian (Stato da Màr: "1480–1797"); the page does not name the previous holder.
1646: in the Candia War the Ottomans attack; the page dates the war 1645-1669 and the 1646 captures.
1646: as the page words it (Krk and Cres are unusual Ottoman conquests, see notes); Stato da Màr confirms a "brief Ottoman occupation" of Krk, Pag and Cres in the Cretan War.
1647: "The following year, the Venetian commander Leonardo Foscolo retook Novigrad."
Stato da Màr: Krk, Pag and Cres were under a "brief Ottoman occupation during the Cretan War (1645–1669)"; neither page dates the end, so the return is bridged to the year Novigrad was retaken.
1669: the peace of the Candia War ends the fighting in Dalmatia.
1669: the territory "had roughly tripled" by the peace.
October 1684: Venice, which had declared war on 25 April 1684, besieges Sinj without success (again in March-April 1685); Sinj falls on 30 September 1686.
30 September 1686: the Venetians take Sinj.
September 1687: Herceg Novi falls to Venice.
11 September 1688: Knin falls, which "ended the inland Dalmatian expansion".
26 November 1690: Venice takes Vrgorac, opening the route toward Imotski and Mostar.
1694: Venice takes the land north of the Republic of Ragusa.
26 January 1699: the Treaty of Karlowitz ends the Morean War.
26 January 1699: Venice cedes the three districts to keep the existing border near Ragusa; the page does not name the receiving state (the Ottomans, by the researcher's reading).
1718: the Treaty of Passarowitz gives Venice Sinj and Imotski ("Sebastiano Mocenigo").
1718: "Čitluk and Gabela were lost to the Ottomans under this treaty."
17 October 1797: by the Treaty of Campo Formio "Venetian Istria, Venetian Dalmatia and the Bay of Kotor region were turned over to the Habsburg emperor"; the Republic of Venice itself is ended.

wars.name: Venetian conquest of Dalmatia against Sigismund
wars.outcome: Venice bought Ladislaus's rights in 1409, beat Sigismund's forces at Motta in 1412 and held the coastal cities by 1420, except Ragusa.

wars.name: Candia War
wars.outcome: The Ottomans took Krk, Pag, Cres and Novigrad in 1646; the peace of 1669 left Venice's territory roughly tripled.

wars.name: Morean War
wars.outcome: Venice took Sinj (1686), Herceg Novi (1687), Knin (1688), Vrgorac (1690) and the land north of Ragusa (1694); at Karlowitz (26 January 1699) it gave up Popovo polje, Klek and Sutorina.

wars.name: Second Morean War (Ottoman-Venetian war of 1714-1718)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans reclaimed the Morea in 1715; in 1718 Venice gained Sinj and Imotski and lost Čitluk and Gabela.

certainty.note: Coastal cities and islands with hinterlands as the Ottoman front moved; no surveyed line on the pages opened.
The Dalmatia-Bosnia border was fixed by Karlowitz (1699) and adjusted at Passarowitz (1718); the page says Knin 1688 "helped set the Dalmatia-Bosnia border that exists today".
